newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Tropical timber pact to go into force in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Tropical timber pact to go into force in 1997.

text.p: Nearly 40 countries agreed on Friday that a tropical timber pact to promote sustainable management of forests would go into effect from January 1997.
The pact was originally due to enter into force from February 1995 after two years of difficult negotiation were completed in early 1994.
But implementation was delayed because not enough countries -- including key powers like the United States and Brazil -- had either signed or ratified.
At a short open meeting at the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD), countries present unanimously agreed on the pact's provisional entry into force.
UNCTAD analysts said this formula, rather than a definitive implementation, was a technicality making it easier for other states which had not signed or ratified to join later.

At the meeting Brazil, which had been critical of the accord because it only covered tropical timber forests and not those in temperate zones, said it would sign up. (Geneva newsroom - 41-22 733-38-31)
